Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space, including dimension zero. Let V:E→ℝ be C², α,β≥0 and η∈ℝ with α>0, α≤β, α‖v‖²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤β‖v‖² for every x,v∈E, η>0 and βη≤1. The following literal constructions are made for all y,r∈E and initial phases z₀∈E×E; the existential process witness below is global in these parameters. Put c=y−η∇V(r), Φ_t(x,p)=(c+cos(t)(x−c)+√η sin(t)p, −sin(t)(x−c)/√η+cos(t)p), g_r(x)=∇V(x)−∇V(r), S_r(x,p)=(x,p−2〈p,g_r(x)〉g_r(x)/‖g_r(x)‖²), λ_r(x,p)=√η max{0,〈p,g_r(x)〉}, Λ_z(t)=∫₀ᵗλ_r(Φ_s(z))ds and τ_z(e)=inf{t≥0:Λ_z(t)≥e}∈[0,∞], with inf empty=∞. Total real division makes S_r the identity at g_r(x)=0. The record space is D=([0,∞)×(E×E))⊕{stopped}, with Borel sum structure. Define next(e,stopped)=stopped; for a live record (T,z), next(e,(T,z))=stopped if τ_z(e)=∞, and otherwise next(e,(T,z))=(T+τ_z(e),S_rΦ_(τ_z(e))(z)). In the Lean definition untopD0 is used only in this non-top branch. Define R₀(e)=live(0,z₀) and R_(j+1)(e)=next(e_j,R_j(e)). Let Ω=ℝ^ℕ with its product Borel structure and P=⊗_(k≥0)Exp(1). Let ε(w)_k=max{w_k,0}; this is an ambient coordinate extension on a P-null nonpositive-clock set, not new source dynamics for negative clocks. 
Write T_j(w)=a for a live record R_j(ε(w))=live(a,z), and T_j(w)=∞ for a stopped record. Define I_n(T)={T_n≤T<T_(n+1)}, and the total selector N(T,w)=min{n:w∈I_n(T)} when such an n exists, and 0 otherwise. For n≥0 let Hist_n=D^(Fin(n+1)) and H_n(w)_j=R_j(ε(w)). Write readTime(live(a,z))=a and readTime(stopped)=0. The abstract guard A_n(T) consists of histories all of whose records are live, whose read times are strictly increasing and whose positive-index read times are strictly below T; it does not constrain record0 itself. Actual H_n starts at live(0,z₀). For h∈Hist_n set d_n(T,h)=max{T−readTime(h_n),0}. Define survival(live(a,z),u,e) to mean u<τ_z(max{e,0}); on stopped it is false. Define W(live(a,z),u)=exp(−Λ_z(u)); on stopped W=0. Put C_n(T)={w:H_n(w)∈A_n(T), survival(R_n(ε(w)),d_n(T,H_n(w)),w_n)}.
For a fixed finite T≥0 let Path_T be all functions from [0,T] into E×E, with its coordinate-product sigma algebra. On every history, including unrealizable ones, define Ψ_n(T,h)(s) by starting at z₀ and visiting j=0,…,n in increasing order: a live record (a,z) with a≤s replaces the current value by Φ_(s−a)(z), and an ineligible live or stopped record leaves it unchanged. All elapsed times in this total definition use nonnegative subtraction.
Define Δ_n(T)={t∈ℝ^n:0<t₁<⋯<t_n<T}, and let m_n be the comap of product Lebesgue measure to this subtype, without normalization. For t∈Δ_n(T), put s₀=0,s_i=t_i, z₀ equal to the prescribed initial phase and z_i=S_rΦ_(s_i−s_(i−1))(z_(i−1)). Set K_n(t)_j=live(s_j,z_j), Γ_n(T,t)=Ψ_n(T,K_n(t)), q_n(t)=ofReal(∏_(i=1)^n λ_r(Φ_(s_i−s_(i−1))(z_(i−1)))exp[−Λ_(z_(i−1))(s_i−s_(i−1))]), and ρ_n(T,t)=q_n(t)W(K_n(t)_n,d_n(T,K_n(t))). The literal toNNReal conversions agree with these nonnegative simplex times.
There exists one actual phase representative Z(y,r,z₀,t,w), jointly Borel in all deterministic parameters, finite time and raw input, with the following properties. On every raw covering interval T_n(w)≤s<T_(n+1)(w), if R_n(ε(w))=live(a,z), then Z(s,w)=Φ_(s−a)(z). If no interval covers s, Z(s,w)=z₀. For each fixed parameter tuple, Z(0,w)=z₀ almost surely.

Put R(x,p)=(x,-p), V_y(x)=V(x)+||x-y||^2/(2 eta), and nu_y=(volume_E.tilted(-V_y)) times stdGaussian(E), in position/momentum order. Here tilted(-V_y) has density ofReal(exp(-V_y(x))/integral exp(-V_y) dx), and stdGaussian is the centered identity-covariance Gaussian. Normalizability is a consequence, not a premise.
For the same single actual Z described above, every y,r in E and every finite T>=0, define for each n in Nat the map B_n(z,t)=(z,Gamma_(y,r,z,n,T,t)(T)), the measure sigma_n=(nu_y times m_n,T).withDensity((z,t)->rho_(y,r,z,n,T)(t)), and L_n=map B_n sigma_n on (E times E) times (E times E). Define M_Z(z,w)=(z,Z(y,r,z,T,w)), Q=map M_Z (nu_y times P), and J(z0,zT)=(R(zT),R(z0)). Every product uses initial phase first, and Q is the actual endpoint-pair law of the specified clock process.
Then simultaneously Q=Measure.sum(n in Nat -> L_n), Q is a probability measure, and J is measurable with map J Q=Q. The sum includes every nonnegative integer without a cap. There is no assumption that a fixed-count sector has mass one. Joint measurability, simplex sigma-finiteness, measurable initial-phase sector integrals, countable exchange, and probability of the input measures are internal dependencies, not supplied hypotheses. In particular no joint-in-initial-state measurability of N is assumed: the count partition is taken at each fixed initial state before nonnegative integration against nu_y.
The conclusion includes n=0 in the sum, T=0, dimension zero, zero rates and infinite waits with the explicit raw exceptional fallback above. At T=0 the actual initialization is almost sure; no pointwise all-clock initialization or jumpwise reversed-path equality is added. Arbitrary nonnegative measurable test functions may have infinite integrals during assembly. Signed bilinear duality, marginal phase invariance, restart/Markovness, hypocoercivity, implementation error, unbounded expected oracle cost and complete paper/composition results remain separate obligations.

{E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    {V : E → ℝ} {α β : ℝ≥0} {η : ℝ}
    (hα : 0 < (α : ℝ)) (hαβ : α ≤ β) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)
    (hH : ∀ x v : E,
      (α : ℝ) * ‖v‖ ^ 2 ≤ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ∧
      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ≤ (β : ℝ) * ‖v‖ ^ 2)
    (hη : 0 < η) (hβη : (β : ℝ) * η ≤ 1) :
    let c : E → E → E := fun y xRef => y - η • gradient V xRef
    let Φ : E → E → ℝ → (E × E) → (E × E) := fun y xRef t z =>
      (c y xRef + Real.cos t • (z.1 - c y xRef) +
          (Real.sqrt η * Real.sin t) • z.2,
       (-Real.sin t / Real.sqrt η) • (z.1 - c y xRef) + Real.cos t • z.2)
    let S : E → (E × E) → (E × E) := fun xRef z =>
      (z.1, z.2 - (2 * inner ℝ z.2 (gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef) /
        ‖gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef‖ ^ 2) • (gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef))
    let rate : E → (E × E) → ℝ := fun xRef z =>
      Real.sqrt η * max 0 (inner ℝ z.2 (gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef))
    let Λ : E → E → (E × E) → ℝ≥0 → ℝ := fun y xRef z t =>
      ∫ s in (0 : ℝ)..(t : ℝ), rate xRef (Φ y xRef s z)
    let τ : E → E → (E × E) → ℝ≥0 → WithTop ℝ≥0 := fun y xRef z e =>
      MeasureTheory.hittingAfter
        (fun t : ℝ≥0 => fun a : (E × E) × (E × E) × ℝ≥0 =>
          Λ a.1.1 a.1.2 a.2.1 t - (a.2.2 : ℝ))
        (Set.Ici (0 : ℝ)) 0 ((y, xRef), z, e)
    let next : E → E → ℝ≥0 → ((ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) ⊕ Unit) →
        ((ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) ⊕ Unit) := fun y xRef e r =>
      match r with
      | Sum.inr _ => Sum.inr ()
      | Sum.inl a =>
        if τ y xRef a.2 e = ⊤ then Sum.inr () else
          Sum.inl (a.1 + (τ y xRef a.2 e).untopD 0,
            S xRef (Φ y xRef (((τ y xRef a.2 e).untopD 0 : ℝ≥0) : ℝ) a.2))
    let record : E → E → (E × E) → (ℕ → ℝ≥0) → ℕ →
        ((ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) ⊕ Unit) := fun y xRef z₀ e n =>
      Nat.rec (Sum.inl (0, z₀)) (fun k r => next y xRef (e k) r) n
    let P : Measure (ℕ → ℝ) := Measure.infinitePi (fun _ : ℕ => expMeasure (1 : ℝ))
    let ε : (ℕ → ℝ) → ℕ → ℝ≥0 := fun w k => Real.toNNReal (w k)
    let history : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (ℕ → ℝ) →
        (Fin (n + 1) → ((ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) ⊕ Unit)) :=
      fun y xRef z₀ n w j => record y xRef z₀ (ε w) j.val
    let Rec := (ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) ⊕ Unit
    let Hist : ℕ → Type _ := fun n => Fin (n + 1) → Rec
    let readTime : Rec → ℝ := fun r => match r with
      | Sum.inl q => (q.1 : ℝ)
      | Sum.inr _ => 0
    let Δ : (n : ℕ) → ℝ≥0 → Set (Fin n → ℝ) := fun n T =>
      {t | StrictMono (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t) ∧ ∀ i, t i < (T : ℝ)}
    let Prefix : (n : ℕ) → ℝ≥0 → Type := fun n T => {t : Fin n → ℝ // t ∈ Δ n T}
    let m : (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) → Measure (Prefix n T) := fun n T =>
      Measure.comap (fun t : Prefix n T => t.val) (volume : Measure (Fin n → ℝ))
    let zAt : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) →
        Prefix n T → Fin (n + 1) → (E × E) := fun y xRef z₀ n T t =>
      Fin.induction z₀ (fun i z =>
        S xRef (Φ y xRef (t.val i - (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (t.val : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i.castSucc) z))
    let K : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) →
        Prefix n T → Hist n := fun y xRef z₀ n T t j =>
      Sum.inl (Real.toNNReal ((Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (t.val : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) j), zAt y xRef z₀ n T t j)
    let qReal : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) →
        Prefix n T → ℝ := fun y xRef z₀ n T t =>
      ∏ i : Fin n,
        rate xRef (Φ y xRef (t.val i - (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (t.val : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i.castSucc)
          (zAt y xRef z₀ n T t i.castSucc)) *
        Real.exp (-Λ y xRef (zAt y xRef z₀ n T t i.castSucc)
          (Real.toNNReal (t.val i - (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (t.val : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i.castSucc)))
    let q : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) →
        Prefix n T → ℝ≥0∞ := fun y xRef z₀ n T t =>
      ENNReal.ofReal (qReal y xRef z₀ n T t)
    let A : (n : ℕ) → ℝ≥0 → Set (Hist n) := fun n T =>
      {h | (∀ j, ∃ a : ℝ≥0 × (E × E), h j = Sum.inl a) ∧
        StrictMono (fun j => readTime (h j)) ∧
        ∀ i : Fin n, readTime (h i.succ) < (T : ℝ)}
    let eventTime : E → E → (E × E) → (ℕ → ℝ) → ℕ → WithTop ℝ≥0 :=
      fun y xRef z₀ w j => (record y xRef z₀ (ε w) j).elim
        (fun a => (a.1 : WithTop ℝ≥0)) (fun _ => ⊤)
    let I : E → E → (E × E) → ℝ≥0 → ℕ → Set (ℕ → ℝ) :=
      fun y xRef z₀ T n => {w | eventTime y xRef z₀ w n ≤ (T : WithTop ℝ≥0) ∧
        (T : WithTop ℝ≥0) < eventTime y xRef z₀ w (n + 1)}
    let N : E → E → (E × E) → ℝ≥0 → (ℕ → ℝ) → ℕ := fun y xRef z₀ T w =>
      if h : ∃ n, w ∈ I y xRef z₀ T n then Nat.find h else 0
    let liveTime : Rec → ℝ≥0 := fun r => r.elim Prod.fst (fun _ => 0)
    let d : (n : ℕ) → ℝ≥0 → Hist n → ℝ≥0 :=
      fun n T h => T - liveTime (h ⟨n, Nat.lt_succ_self n⟩)
    let survival : E → E → Rec → ℝ≥0 → ℝ → Prop :=
      fun y xRef r u e => r.elim
        (fun a => (u : WithTop ℝ≥0) < τ y xRef a.2 (Real.toNNReal e)) (fun _ => False)
    let weight : E → E → Rec → ℝ≥0 → ℝ≥0∞ :=
      fun y xRef r u => r.elim
        (fun a => ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (-Λ y xRef a.2 u))) (fun _ => 0)
    let C : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → ℝ≥0 → Set (ℕ → ℝ) :=
      fun y xRef z₀ n T => {w | history y xRef z₀ n w ∈ A n T ∧
        survival y xRef (record y xRef z₀ (ε w) n) (d n T (history y xRef z₀ n w)) (w n)}
    let Path : ℝ≥0 → Type _ := fun T => {s : ℝ≥0 // s ≤ T} → E × E
    let Ψ : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) → Hist n → Path T :=
      fun y xRef z₀ n T h s =>
        Fin.foldl (n + 1) (fun z j => (h j).elim
          (fun a => if a.1 ≤ s.val then Φ y xRef ((s.val - a.1 : ℝ≥0) : ℝ) a.2 else z)
          (fun _ => z)) z₀
    let Γ : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) → Prefix n T → Path T :=
      fun y xRef z₀ n T t => Ψ y xRef z₀ n T (K y xRef z₀ n T t)
    let ρ : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) → Prefix n T → ℝ≥0∞ :=
      fun y xRef z₀ n T t => q y xRef z₀ n T t *
        weight y xRef ((K y xRef z₀ n T t) ⟨n, Nat.lt_succ_self n⟩)
          (d n T (K y xRef z₀ n T t))
    let R : E × E → E × E := fun z => (z.1, -z.2)
    let Vy : E → E → ℝ := fun y x => V x + ‖x - y‖ ^ 2 / (2 * η)
    let nu : E → Measure (E × E) := fun y =>
      ((volume : Measure E).tilted (fun x => -Vy y x)).prod
        (ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian E)
    ∃ Z : E → E → (E × E) → ℝ≥0 → (ℕ → ℝ) → (E × E),
      Measurable (fun a : ((E × E) × (E × E)) × ℝ≥0 × (ℕ → ℝ) =>
        Z a.1.1.1 a.1.1.2 a.1.2 a.2.1 a.2.2) ∧
      (∀ y xRef : E, ∀ z₀ : E × E, ∀ w : ℕ → ℝ, ∀ s : ℝ≥0,
        ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ a : ℝ≥0 × (E × E), w ∈ I y xRef z₀ s n →
          record y xRef z₀ (ε w) n = Sum.inl a →
          Z y xRef z₀ s w = Φ y xRef ((s - a.1 : ℝ≥0) : ℝ) a.2) ∧
      (∀ y xRef : E, ∀ z₀ : E × E, ∀ w : ℕ → ℝ, ∀ s : ℝ≥0,
        (¬ ∃ n, w ∈ I y xRef z₀ s n) → Z y xRef z₀ s w = z₀) ∧
      (∀ y xRef : E, ∀ z₀ : E × E, ∀ᵐ w ∂P, Z y xRef z₀ 0 w = z₀) ∧
      (∀ y r : E, ∀ T : ℝ≥0,
        let B : (n : ℕ) → (E × E) × Prefix n T → (E × E) × (E × E) :=
          fun n q => (q.1, Γ y r q.1 n T q.2 ⟨T, le_rfl⟩)
        let sigma : (n : ℕ) → Measure ((E × E) × Prefix n T) := fun n =>
          ((nu y).prod (m n T)).withDensity (fun q => ρ y r q.1 n T q.2)
        let L : ℕ → Measure ((E × E) × (E × E)) := fun n => Measure.map (B n) (sigma n)
        let M : (E × E) × (ℕ → ℝ) → (E × E) × (E × E) :=
          fun q => (q.1, Z y r q.1 T q.2)
        let Q : Measure ((E × E) × (E × E)) := Measure.map M ((nu y).prod P)
        let J : (E × E) × (E × E) → (E × E) × (E × E) :=
          fun q => (R q.2, R q.1)
        Q = Measure.sum L ∧ IsProbabilityMeasure Q ∧ MeasurePreserving J Q Q)
decoder_context: Finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space with canonical volume, including rank zero; genuine second Frechet derivative and real Hilbert gradient.
Fin n is zero-based; Fin.cons prepends; Fin.induction constructs a finite sequence; Fin.foldl visits ascending indices. Sum.inl represents a live time/state record; Unit represents a stopped record.

Real division by zero is zero; Real.toNNReal is positive part; nonnegative subtraction is truncated. ENNReal.ofReal embeds the positive part in extended nonnegative reals. Interval integrals use real Lebesgue measure.

Measure.tilted mu h is mu.withDensity(x -> ofReal(exp(h(x))/integral exp(h) dmu)). stdGaussian E is the centered identity-covariance Gaussian. Measure.comap along a measurable subtype inclusion is the induced subtype measure. Products use the displayed coordinate order.

MeasurePreserving f mu nu states Measurable f and Measure.map f mu = nu. withDensity multiplies the base measure by the given extended-nonnegative density. Measure.sum is the countable sum of the displayed measures. IsProbabilityMeasure means total mass one. All literal let bindings are definitions, not hypotheses.

hittingAfter f D 0 a is the infimum of nonnegative times t at which f t a lies in D, in WithTop nonnegative reals; the empty infimum is top. untopD 0 returns the finite value when not top and zero otherwise.

Measure.infinitePi constructs the displayed countable product law; expMeasure 1 is the unit-rate exponential probability measure on real numbers. The function space carries the coordinate-product measurable structure. A measurable global process and its almost-everywhere initialization are conclusions.

    let Δ : (n : ℕ) → ℝ≥0 → Set (Fin n → ℝ) := fun n T =>

    let K : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) →
        Prefix n T → Hist n := fun y xRef z₀ n T t j =>
      Sum.inl (Real.toNNReal ((Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (t.val : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) j), zAt y xRef z₀ n T t j)
    let qReal : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) →
        Prefix n T → ℝ := fun y xRef z₀ n T t =>
      ∏ i : Fin n,
        rate xRef (Φ y xRef (t.val i - (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (t.val : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i.castSucc)
          (zAt y xRef z₀ n T t i.castSucc)) *
        Real.exp (-Λ y xRef (zAt y xRef z₀ n T t i.castSucc)
          (Real.toNNReal (t.val i - (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (t.val : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i.castSucc)))
    let q : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) →
        Prefix n T → ℝ≥0∞ := fun y xRef z₀ n T t =>
      ENNReal.ofReal (qReal y xRef z₀ n T t)

    let d : (n : ℕ) → ℝ≥0 → Hist n → ℝ≥0 :=

    let survival : E → E → Rec → ℝ≥0 → ℝ → Prop :=
      fun y xRef r u e => r.elim

    let weight : E → E → Rec → ℝ≥0 → ℝ≥0∞ :=
      fun y xRef r u => r.elim

    let C : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → ℝ≥0 → Set (ℕ → ℝ) :=
      fun y xRef z₀ n T => {w | history y xRef z₀ n w ∈ A n T ∧
        survival y xRef (record y xRef z₀ (ε w) n) (d n T (history y xRef z₀ n w)) (w n)}
    let Path : ℝ≥0 → Type _ := fun T => {s : ℝ≥0 // s ≤ T} → E × E
    let Ψ : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) → Hist n → Path T :=
      fun y xRef z₀ n T h s =>
        Fin.foldl (n + 1) (fun z j => (h j).elim
          (fun a => if a.1 ≤ s.val then Φ y xRef ((s.val - a.1 : ℝ≥0) : ℝ) a.2 else z)

    let Γ : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) → Prefix n T → Path T :=
      fun y xRef z₀ n T t => Ψ y xRef z₀ n T (K y xRef z₀ n T t)
    let ρ : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) → Prefix n T → ℝ≥0∞ :=
      fun y xRef z₀ n T t => q y xRef z₀ n T t *
        weight y xRef ((K y xRef z₀ n T t) ⟨n, Nat.lt_succ_self n⟩)
          (d n T (K y xRef z₀ n T t))
    let R : E × E → E × E := fun z => (z.1, -z.2)
    let Vy : E → E → ℝ := fun y x => V x + ‖x - y‖ ^ 2 / (2 * η)
    let nu : E → Measure (E × E) := fun y =>
      ((volume : Measure E).tilted (fun x => -Vy y x)).prod
        (ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian E)
    ∃ Z : E → E → (E × E) → ℝ≥0 → (ℕ → ℝ) → (E × E),
      Measurable (fun a : ((E × E) × (E × E)) × ℝ≥0 × (ℕ → ℝ) =>
        Z a.1.1.1 a.1.1.2 a.1.2 a.2.1 a.2.2) ∧
      (∀ y xRef : E, ∀ z₀ : E × E, ∀ w : ℕ → ℝ, ∀ s : ℝ≥0,
        ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ a : ℝ≥0 × (E × E), w ∈ I y xRef z₀ s n →
          record y xRef z₀ (ε w) n = Sum.inl a →
          Z y xRef z₀ s w = Φ y xRef ((s - a.1 : ℝ≥0) : ℝ) a.2) ∧
      (∀ y xRef : E, ∀ z₀ : E × E, ∀ w : ℕ → ℝ, ∀ s : ℝ≥0,
        (¬ ∃ n, w ∈ I y xRef z₀ s n) → Z y xRef z₀ s w = z₀) ∧
      (∀ y xRef : E, ∀ z₀ : E × E, ∀ᵐ w ∂P, Z y xRef z₀ 0 w = z₀) ∧
      (∀ y r : E, ∀ T : ℝ≥0,
        let B : (n : ℕ) → (E × E) × Prefix n T → (E × E) × (E × E) :=
          fun n q => (q.1, Γ y r q.1 n T q.2 ⟨T, le_rfl⟩)
        let sigma : (n : ℕ) → Measure ((E × E) × Prefix n T) := fun n =>
          ((nu y).prod (m n T)).withDensity (fun q => ρ y r q.1 n T q.2)
        let L : ℕ → Measure ((E × E) × (E × E)) := fun n => Measure.map (B n) (sigma n)
        let M : (E × E) × (ℕ → ℝ) → (E × E) × (E × E) :=
          fun q => (q.1, Z y r q.1 T q.2)
        let Q : Measure ((E × E) × (E × E)) := Measure.map M ((nu y).prod P)
        let J : (E × E) × (E × E) → (E × E) × (E × E) :=
          fun q => (R q.2, R q.1)
        Q = Measure.sum L ∧ IsProbabilityMeasure Q ∧ MeasurePreserving J Q Q)

/-- The actual Gibbs-initialized endpoint law is the countable sector sum, a probability, and preserved by the flipped swap. -/
theorem actual_countable_endpoint_law
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    {V : E → ℝ} {α β : ℝ≥0} {η : ℝ}
    (hα : 0 < (α : ℝ)) (hαβ : α ≤ β) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)
    (hH : ∀ x v : E,
      (α : ℝ) * ‖v‖ ^ 2 ≤ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ∧
      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ≤ (β : ℝ) * ‖v‖ ^ 2)
    (hη : 0 < η) (hβη : (β : ℝ) * η ≤ 1) : actual_countable_endpoint_statement hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη := by
  classical
  unfold actual_countable_endpoint_statement
  intro c Φ S rate Λ τ next record P ε history Rec Hist readTime Δ Prefix m zAt K qReal q A eventTime I N liveTime d survival weight C Path Ψ Γ ρ R Vy nu
  obtain ⟨Z, hZm, hZa, hZf, hZ0, h93⟩ :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.ProximalBPS.ActualFiniteCountPath.actual_finite_count_path_law
      hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη
  refine ⟨Z, hZm, hZa, hZf, hZ0, ?_⟩
  intro y r T B sigma L M Q J
  have h103 := AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.ProximalBPS.ActualPhaseNormalization.actual_phase_gibbs_normalization
    hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη y
  letI : IsProbabilityMeasure (nu y) := by
    have hp := h103.2.2.2.2.2.1
    rw [h103.2.2.2.2.2.2] at hp
    exact hp
  letI : IsProbabilityMeasure P :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.UnitExponentialProduct.unit_exponential_product_laws.1
  have hembZ : Measurable (fun q : (E × E) × (ℕ → ℝ) => (((y, r), q.1), T, q.2)) :=
    (measurable_const.prodMk measurable_fst).prodMk (measurable_const.prodMk measurable_snd)
  have hZend := hZm.comp hembZ
  have hM : Measurable M := measurable_fst.prodMk hZend
  have hQ : IsProbabilityMeasure Q := Measure.isProbabilityMeasure_map hM.aemeasurable
  have hB (n : ℕ) : Measurable (B n) := by
    have hemb : Measurable (fun q : (E × E) × Prefix n T => (((y, r), q.1), q.2)) :=
      (measurable_const.prodMk measurable_fst).prodMk measurable_snd
    have hp := (h93 n T).2.1.comp hemb
    have he := (measurable_pi_apply (⟨T, le_rfl⟩ : {s : ℝ≥0 // s ≤ T})).comp hp
    exact measurable_fst.prodMk he
  have hρ (n : ℕ) : Measurable (fun q : (E × E) × Prefix n T => ρ y r q.1 n T q.2) := by
    have hemb : Measurable (fun q : (E × E) × Prefix n T => (((y, r), q.1), q.2)) :=
      (measurable_const.prodMk measurable_fst).prodMk measurable_snd
    have h := (h93 n T).2.2.1.comp hemb
    simpa only [Function.comp_def] using h
  have hm (n : ℕ) : SigmaFinite (m n T) := by
    have hcons (i : Fin (n + 1)) :
        Measurable (fun t : Fin n → ℝ => (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i) := by
      induction i using Fin.cases with
      | zero => exact measurable_const
      | succ i => exact measurable_pi_apply i
    have hs : MeasurableSet (Δ n T) := by
      change MeasurableSet {t : Fin n → ℝ |
        (∀ i j : Fin (n + 1), i < j → (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i < (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) j) ∧
        ∀ i : Fin n, t i < (T : ℝ)}
      rw [Set.ofPred_and]
      apply MeasurableSet.inter
      · simpa only [← Set.ofPred_forall] using (MeasurableSet.iInter fun (i : Fin (n + 1)) =>
          MeasurableSet.iInter fun (j : Fin (n + 1)) =>
          MeasurableSet.iInter fun (_ : i < j) => measurableSet_lt (hcons i) (hcons j))
      · simpa only [← Set.ofPred_forall] using (MeasurableSet.iInter fun (i : Fin n) =>
          measurableSet_lt (measurable_pi_apply i) (measurable_const (a := (T : ℝ))))
    have hmσ : SigmaFinite ((m n T).map (fun t : Prefix n T => t.val)) := by
      change SigmaFinite ((Measure.comap (fun t : Prefix n T => t.val)
        (volume : Measure (Fin n → ℝ))).map (fun t : Prefix n T => t.val))
      rw [map_comap_subtype_coe hs]
      infer_instance
    exact SigmaFinite.of_map (m n T) measurable_subtype_coe.aemeasurable hmσ
  have hsum : Q = Measure.sum L := by
    apply Measure.ext_of_lintegral
    intro F hF
    let D : ℕ → (E × E) → ℝ≥0∞ := fun n z =>
      ∫⁻ t : Prefix n T, F (B n (z, t)) * ρ y r z n T t ∂m n T
    have hD (n : ℕ) : Measurable (D n) := by
      letI := hm n
      exact ((hF.comp (hB n)).mul (hρ n)).lintegral_prod_right'
    have hz (z : E × E) :
        (∫⁻ w, F (z, Z y r z T w) ∂P) = ∑' n, D n z := by
      have hN : Measurable (N y r z T) := ((h93 0 T).2.2.2 y r z).2.2.1
      have hsets (n : ℕ) : MeasurableSet {w | N y r z T w = n} :=
        (measurableSet_singleton n).preimage hN
      have hdis : Pairwise (fun i j : ℕ => Disjoint {w | N y r z T w = i} {w | N y r z T w = j}) := by
        intro i j hij
        exact Set.disjoint_left.mpr (fun w hi hj => hij (hi.symm.trans hj))
      have hu : (⋃ n : ℕ, {w | N y r z T w = n}) = Set.univ := by
        ext w
        simp
      calc
        (∫⁻ w, F (z, Z y r z T w) ∂P) =
            ∑' n, ∫⁻ w in {w | N y r z T w = n}, F (z, Z y r z T w) ∂P := by
          simpa only [hu, Measure.restrict_univ] using
            (lintegral_iUnion hsets hdis (fun w => F (z, Z y r z T w)))
        _ = ∑' n, D n z := by
          apply tsum_congr
          intro n
          rcases (h93 n T).2.2.2 y r z with
            ⟨hH, hZT, hNN, hC, hGamma, hactual, hAE, hdisjoint, hcover, hlaw, hint, hmass, hbound⟩
          exact hint (fun hp => F (z, hp.2 ⟨T, le_rfl⟩))
            (hF.comp (measurable_const.prodMk ((measurable_pi_apply (⟨T, le_rfl⟩ : {s : ℝ≥0 // s ≤ T})).comp measurable_snd)))
    calc
      (∫⁻ x, F x ∂Q) = ∫⁻ z, ∫⁻ w, F (z, Z y r z T w) ∂P ∂nu y := by
        change (∫⁻ x, F x ∂Measure.map M ((nu y).prod P)) = _
        rw [lintegral_map hF hM]
        exact lintegral_prod (f := fun x => F (M x)) (hF.comp hM).aemeasurable
      _ = ∫⁻ z, ∑' n, D n z ∂nu y := lintegral_congr hz
      _ = ∑' n, ∫⁻ z, D n z ∂nu y := lintegral_tsum (fun n => (hD n).aemeasurable)
      _ = ∑' n, ∫⁻ x, F x ∂L n := by
        apply tsum_congr
        intro n
        letI := hm n
        change (∫⁻ z, ∫⁻ t : Prefix n T, F (B n (z, t)) * ρ y r z n T t ∂m n T ∂nu y) =
          ∫⁻ x, F x ∂Measure.map (B n) (sigma n)
        rw [lintegral_map hF (hB n)]
        change _ = ∫⁻ x, F (B n x) ∂(((nu y).prod (m n T)).withDensity (fun x => ρ y r x.1 n T x.2))
        rw [lintegral_withDensity_eq_lintegral_mul _
          (f := fun x : (E × E) × Prefix n T => ρ y r x.1 n T x.2)
          (g := fun x => F (B n x)) (hρ n) (hF.comp (hB n))]
        simp only [Pi.mul_apply]
        rw [lintegral_prod (f := fun x : (E × E) × Prefix n T =>
          ρ y r x.1 n T x.2 * F (B n x)) ((hρ n).mul (hF.comp (hB n))).aemeasurable]
        apply lintegral_congr
        intro z
        apply lintegral_congr
        intro t
        exact mul_comm _ _
      _ = ∫⁻ x, F x ∂Measure.sum L := (lintegral_sum_measure F L).symm
  have hsector (n : ℕ) : MeasurePreserving J (L n) (L n) :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.ProximalBPS.ActualNormalizedEndpointSector.actual_normalized_endpoint_sector_reversal
      hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη y r n T
  refine ⟨hsum, hQ, (hsector 0).measurable, ?_⟩
  rw [hsum, Measure.map_sum (hsector 0).measurable.aemeasurable]
  congr 1
  funext n
  exact (hsector n).map_eq

end

On every raw covering interval T_n(w)≤s<T_(n+1)(w), if R_n(ε(w))=live(a,z), then Z(s,w)=Φ_(s−a)(z). If no interval covers s, Z(s,w)=z₀. For each fixed parameter tuple, Z(0,w)=z₀ almost surely.

reconstruction.text:
Anonymous mathematical reconstruction

Objects, hypotheses, and quantification

Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product space, equipped with its normed additive-group structure and a measurable structure equal to the Borel structure. The dimension is not required to be positive; the zero-dimensional space is included. Use the canonical volume measure on E. Let V:E→R be twice continuously Frechet differentiable. Let α and β be nonnegative real numbers and η be a real number. Assume α>0, α≤β, η>0, βη≤1, and, for every x,v∈E,
    α||v||² ≤ D²V(x)[v,v] ≤ β||v||².
Here D²V is the genuine iterated Frechet derivative and ∇V is the real Hilbert-space gradient. These are all the hypotheses. In particular the definitions and probability/measure assertions below are not additional hypotheses.

All constructions below have V and η fixed; the theorem is universally quantified over E, its displayed structures, V, α, β, η, and proofs of the stated hypotheses. The conclusion supplies one jointly measurable function Z that works simultaneously for every center y, reference point r, initial phase-space state z₀, nonnegative time, and real sequence. The variables y and r range independently over E; no relation between them or z₀ is assumed.

Deterministic flow, reflection, and event recursion

Write z=(x,v)∈E×E, and define c(y,r)=y−η∇V(r). For every real t, set
    Φ(y,r,t,(x,v)) = (
      c(y,r)+cos(t)(x−c(y,r))+sqrt(η) sin(t) v,
      −sin(t)/sqrt(η) (x−c(y,r))+cos(t) v).
Scalar multiplication in these formulas is real scalar multiplication in E. Set g_r(x)=∇V(x)−∇V(r), and define
    S(r,(x,v))=(x, v−[2⟨v,g_r(x)⟩/||g_r(x)||²]g_r(x)),
    rate(r,(x,v))=sqrt(η) max(0,⟨v,g_r(x)⟩).
Real division is totalized, with division by zero equal to zero. Consequently when g_r(x)=0 the reflection fixes (x,v), and its event rate is zero. The hypotheses give sqrt(η)>0, so the flow's displayed division by sqrt(η) is nondegenerate.

For u≥0, define the real integrated rate
    Λ(y,r,z,u)=∫₀ᵘ rate(r,Φ(y,r,s,z)) ds,
where the integral is a real interval integral against Lebesgue measure. For e≥0, define
    τ(y,r,z,e)=inf {u≥0 : Λ(y,r,z,u)−e≥0},
with values in [0,∞], with the infimum of the empty set equal to ∞. This is a hitting-time definition starting at time zero. A finite value is extracted by untopD 0; this operation would return zero on ∞. In particular e=0 has τ=0 since Λ at time zero is zero.

A record is either live, written live(t,z), with t≥0 and z∈E×E, or stopped, written stopped. For a threshold e≥0, next(y,r,e,stopped)=stopped. From live(t,z), next returns stopped if τ(y,r,z,e)=∞; otherwise it returns
    live(t+τ(y,r,z,e), S(r,Φ(y,r,τ(y,r,z,e),z))).
The flow receives the finite waiting time as a real number. For any sequence e:N→[0,∞), define record(y,r,z₀,e,0)=live(0,z₀) and
    record(y,r,z₀,e,k+1)=next(y,r,e(k),record(y,r,z₀,e,k)).
Thus a stopped record remains stopped, and every finite event record contains the state after reflection.

Random input and finite histories

Let Ω=R^N, with the coordinate-product measurable structure, and let P be the countable product of unit-rate exponential probability measures on R. Define ε(w)(k)=max(w(k),0), regarded as a nonnegative real. All pointwise definitions are made for every real sequence w, including sequences with nonpositive coordinates; the probability law P is the specified exponential product law.

For n∈N, Hist(n) is the space of sequences of n+1 records, indexed by 0,...,n. Define
    history(y,r,z₀,n,w)(j)=record(y,r,z₀,ε(w),j).
For a live record define readTime(live(t,z))=t as a real number and liveTime(live(t,z))=t as a nonnegative real number. Both functions return zero on stopped.

For T≥0, let Δ(n,T) consist of real n-tuples t=(t₁,...,t_n) such that the prepended sequence (0,t₁,...,t_n) is strictly increasing and every t_i<T. Let Prefix(n,T) be this set as a subtype. For n≥1 this means 0<t₁<⋯<t_n<T. For n=0 the tuple is empty and both conditions are vacuous, including when T=0. The measure m(n,T) is the induced subtype measure obtained by comapping Lebesgue volume on R^n along the inclusion of Prefix(n,T).

For a prefix put t₀=0, z₀ equal to the given initial state, and recursively for i=1,...,n put
    δ_i=t_i−t_(i−1),
    z_i=S(r,Φ(y,r,δ_i,z_(i−1))).
This finite sequence is zAt. Its associated history K(y,r,z₀,n,T,t) is (live(t_j,z_j))_(j=0,...,n); the literal definition converts each real t_j to its nonnegative part. These conversions have no effect on a valid prefix.

Define the real and extended-nonnegative prefix densities by
    qReal(y,r,z₀,n,T,t)=Π_(i=1)^n [
      rate(r,Φ(y,r,δ_i,z_(i−1))) exp(−Λ(y,r,z_(i−1),max(δ_i,0)))],
    q(y,r,z₀,n,T,t)=ofReal(qReal(y,r,z₀,n,T,t)).
The exponential factor is inside the product, one factor for each event. The increments are strictly positive on a valid nonempty prefix. The empty product for n=0 is one. The operation ofReal embeds the nonnegative part of a real number in [0,∞].

Let A(n,T) be the set of arbitrary histories h∈Hist(n) for which every record is live, their readTime values are strictly increasing, and the records with indices 1,...,n have readTime<T. The condition defining A does not itself prescribe a zero initial record time, an initial state, or the state recursion. Those properties belong to history or K where applicable. For n=0, membership in A only requires that the sole record be live, so there is no strict horizon test on its time.

Define eventTime(y,r,z₀,w,j) to be the cumulative time of the j-th record if that record is live, and ∞ if it is stopped. Define
    I(y,r,z₀,T,n)={w : eventTime(w,n)≤T<eventTime(w,n+1)},
using the displayed fixed parameters in the event times and inequalities in [0,∞]. Thus equality of the n-th event time to T is permitted, and equality of the next event time to T is excluded. Define N(y,r,z₀,T,w) as the least natural number n for which w belongs to I(y,r,z₀,T,n), if any such n exists, and as zero otherwise. This is a totalized definition; the final assertions do not separately state a theorem about N.

For an arbitrary history h define
    d(n,T,h)=T−liveTime(h_n)
in nonnegative reals, so this subtraction is truncated at zero. For a record a, u≥0, and real e define survival(y,r,a,u,e) by the following cases: it is u<τ(y,r,z,max(e,0)) when a=live(t,z), and is false when a=stopped. Also define
    weight(y,r,live(t,z),u)=ofReal(exp(−Λ(y,r,z,u))),
    weight(y,r,stopped,u)=0.
The cumulative time t of a live record is not an argument to the rate integral in these two definitions. Define C(y,r,z₀,n,T) as the set of w such that history(y,r,z₀,n,w) lies in A(n,T) and survival holds for the n-th record, residual duration d(n,T,history(y,r,z₀,n,w)), and threshold w(n). C is defined in the statement, but no separate identity or probability formula about C is asserted in the conclusion.

Path reconstruction and full density

Path(T) is the space of all functions [0,T]→E×E, with time represented by nonnegative reals at most T. For an arbitrary history h, define Ψ(y,r,z₀,n,T,h)(s) by starting with accumulator z₀, visiting indices j=0,...,n in ascending order, and applying the following update. If h_j=live(t_j,z_j) and t_j≤s, replace the accumulator with Φ(y,r,s−t_j,z_j), where subtraction is nonnegative truncated subtraction. If that record is stopped or its time exceeds s, keep the accumulator. Thus the final result uses the last eligible index in the finite sequence; arbitrary histories need not be ordered. If no index is eligible the value is z₀.

Define Γ(y,r,z₀,n,T,t)=Ψ(y,r,z₀,n,T,K(y,r,z₀,n,T,t)). For a valid prefix it follows the prescribed flow from each recorded state between successive times and uses the post-reflection state at an event time. Define
    ρ(y,r,z₀,n,T,t)=q(y,r,z₀,n,T,t)
      ·weight(y,r,K(y,r,z₀,n,T,t)_n,d(n,T,K(y,r,z₀,n,T,t))).
Equivalently on valid prefixes this is the product of all n event-rate/exponential factors above multiplied by exp(−Λ(y,r,z_n,T−t_n)), embedded in the extended nonnegative reals. For n=0 it is exp(−Λ(y,r,z₀,T)) with that same embedding. Prefixes exclude events exactly at T when n≥1; the event-index definition I uses the distinct weak/strict inequalities given above.

Initial-state measure and reversal

Define R(x,v)=(x,−v). For each y∈E define
    V_y(x)=V(x)+||x−y||²/(2η),
    H_y=∫_E exp(−V_y(x)) dvolume(x).
The position measure is volume tilted by −V_y, meaning the density with respect to volume is
    ofReal(exp(−V_y(x))/H_y).
Define ν_y to be the product of this position measure and the centered identity-covariance Gaussian on E, in position-then-velocity coordinate order. The normalization uses the real integral and totalized real division; positivity or finiteness of H_y is not an extra hypothesis in the supplied statement. In particular the definition itself would give a zero density if its real normalization value were zero. The theorem makes its probability assertion in the conclusion below.

Exact existential conclusion

There exists a function
    Z:E→E→(E×E)→[0,∞)→Ω→(E×E)
with all of the following properties simultaneously.

1. Joint measurability: the function (y,r,z₀,s,w)↦Z(y,r,z₀,s,w) is measurable for the displayed product measurable structures and the Borel structure on E×E. The Lean tuple grouping is ((y,r),z₀) paired with (s,w).

2. Pointwise interpolation: for every y,r,z₀,w,s≥0 in their respective domains, every n∈N, and every live record a=(t,z), if w∈I(y,r,z₀,s,n) and record(y,r,z₀,ε(w),n)=live(t,z), then
    Z(y,r,z₀,s,w)=Φ(y,r,s−t,z),
where the time difference is nonnegative truncated subtraction. This is an everywhere quantified implication, not merely an almost-everywhere statement.

3. Pointwise fallback: for every y,r,z₀,w,s, if there is no n with w∈I(y,r,z₀,s,n), then Z(y,r,z₀,s,w)=z₀. This covers all exceptional real sequences or times lacking a finite index satisfying the specified event-time bracket. The statement does not replace this fallback by an undefined value or a separate cemetery state for Z.

4. Almost-everywhere initialization: for every fixed y,r,z₀, for P-almost every w,
    Z(y,r,z₀,0,w)=z₀.
The null set may depend on the fixed y,r,z₀; a single universal null set over all those parameters is not asserted. The initialization clause is not stated for every w.

5. Endpoint measure expansion, probability, and reversal: for every y,r∈E and T≥0, make the following definitions. For every n∈N let
    B_n(z,t)=(z,Γ(y,r,z,n,T,t)(T)),
    σ_n=(ν_y×m(n,T)).withDensity((z,t)↦ρ(y,r,z,n,T,t)),
    L_n=(B_n)_*σ_n.
These are measures on ordered pairs of phase-space states after pushing forward. Define
    M(z,w)=(z,Z(y,r,z,T,w)),
    Q=M_*(ν_y×P),
    J(z,z')=(R(z'),R(z)).
Then all three assertions hold:
    Q=Σ_(n=0)^∞ L_n;
    Q has total mass one;
    J is measurable and J_*Q=Q.
The sum is the countable sum of measures, and equality is equality of measures on (E×E)×(E×E). Each L_n uses n strictly positive, strictly ordered event times strictly below T, with the final survival weight. The measure Q is the joint law of initial and time-T states when initial state and threshold sequence are drawn independently from ν_y and P. Reversal both swaps the two endpoint states and negates each velocity. It uses the same y and r on both sides. The theorem's last clause concerns this endpoint measure; it does not separately assert an equality of full path laws, Markovness, uniqueness of Z, a convergence rate, a numerical error bound, or an everywhere finite event count.

Constants, dependence, and edge cases

All numerical constants are the displayed 0, 1, and 2: exponential thresholds have rate 1, the Hessian upper bound is constrained by βη≤1, the reflection coefficient has numerator 2, and the additional potential has denominator 2η. The parameters α and β restrict the theorem's admissible V and η; they do not appear as extra free inputs to Z or in the literal definitions of flow, rates, measures, or densities. Z may depend on the fixed ambient space, V, η, and the theorem's fixed admissible data. There is no hidden dimension lower bound or separate bound on y,r,z₀,T. Times T and s may be zero; η is strictly positive. For n=0 all empty-prefix conventions above apply. No nonexplosion, nonzero gradient-difference, distinctness of y and r, or positivity of individual real coordinates w(k) is an additional assumption. Infinite waiting times, stopped records, zero thresholds, nonpositive raw thresholds, truncated time differences, and absent finite event brackets are handled by the explicit totalized definitions.
